_comment: Declarative E2E fixture dataset. Every agent name starts with 'e2e-test-' so the Playwright suite can discriminate its own fixtures amid any other data in the shared dev DB. session_ids are derived deterministically in seed.py via uuid5(NAMESPACE_FLIGHTDECK, 'flightdeck-e2e/<agent_name>/<role>'), so each seed run addresses the same session rows and idempotency is a per-session HTTP GET.

session_roles._comment: Timeline offsets drive the UI state each fixture tests. Offsets are seconds relative to seed-time. 'aged-closed' and 'stale' require a post-seed SQL backdate because the worker stamps last_seen_at = NOW() regardless of event payload timestamp; see seed.py :: backdate_sessions. 'phase4_extras' (when present) is a list of additional event-shape strings the seeder emits on top of the base session_start / pre_call / post_call / tool_call / session_end timeline. Recognised values: 'embeddings' (no-content), 'embeddings_with_content_string' (has_content=true, single-string input), 'embeddings_with_content_list' (has_content=true, list-of-strings input), 'streaming_post_call', 'streaming_post_call_aborted', 'call_fields_post_call' (a metered post_call carrying every per-call token, serving and cost field), 'prompt_content_post_call' (a captured Anthropic call with JSON-bearing message, tool_use and tool_result blocks for the Prompts panel's Pretty / Raw views), 'llm_error_rate_limit', 'llm_error_context_overflow', 'llm_error_authentication', 'llm_error_timeout', 'policy_warn', 'policy_degrade', 'policy_block', 'mcp_policy_user_remembered' (the Claude Code plugin's remembered MCP approval, with its permission mode), 'signal_context_compacted', 'signal_model_switched', 'signal_notification', 'signal_permission_denied', 'signal_command_expanded', 'signal_task_completed', 'signal_cwd_changed', 'signal_config_changed', 'signal_teammate_idle' and 'signal_elicitation_responded' (Claude Code session_signal events: a compaction with its captured summary, a model switch, an idle-prompt notification, an auto-mode denial, a slash command, a finished teammate task, a directory change, a project settings change, an idle teammate, a declined MCP form), 'history_padding' (25 tool_calls 30 ms apart, so a later extra sits beyond the first 21 events of its session), 'mcp_tool_list', 'mcp_tool_call', 'mcp_tool_call_failed' (mcp_tool_call with structured payload.error — MCPErrorIndicator anchor), 'mcp_resource_list', 'mcp_resource_read', 'mcp_prompt_list', 'mcp_prompt_get'. Other optional role fields: 'force_state' pins the state in the full seed's backdate; 'last_seen_offset_sec' backdates an open run's last_seen_at apart from its started_at; 'event_offset_floor_sec' lets a role post its events further back than the default 1 h clamp (ingestion accepts 48 h); 'fanout_group' ('coordinator' or 'worker') puts an open role in the fan-out refresh, which pins the whole group in one statement on the full seed and every keep-alive cycle; 'skip_subagent_refresh' keeps refresh_subagent_events (T56) off a role whose timestamps must not move.

fresh-active.purpose: T1 LIVE/RECENT bucket; T5 visible in swimlane; T14 embeddings drawer row -- four variants (no-content, captured-string, captured-list-with-content, captured-list-no-content) covering EmbeddingsContentViewer's render branches; T15 happy-path streaming post_call

recent-closed.purpose: T1 RECENT bucket; T5 closed-state badge; T16 carries one llm_error event so the session row's red error-indicator dot appears alongside the closed badge; T126 reads its ten session_signal events (a compaction with a captured summary, a model switch, a notification, an auto-mode denial, a slash command, a finished task, a directory change, a settings change, an idle teammate, a declined MCP form)

aged-closed.purpose: T5 anchor: started 28h ago, ended 27h ago. Must NOT appear in 24h swimlane circles (server filters /v1/sessions by started_at AT fleet.ts::SWIMLANE_LOOKBACK_MS=24h) but MUST appear in expanded drawer via loadExpandedSessions (which fetches with no from/to bound). Plan called for 23h/22h but those values sit INSIDE the 24h window; 28h/27h gives a safe margin either side of the boundary. Requires post-seed SQL backdate AND force_state='closed'.

stale.purpose: T1 non-active state. 3h gap puts it past both the 2-min stale and 10-min lost reconciler thresholds (see workers/internal/writer/postgres.go:543). seed.py pins state='lost' deterministically (matches what the reconciler would set on its next pass) so a freshly-seeded stack is test-stable without waiting for a reconciler tick. Requires post-seed SQL backdate + force_state.

error-active.purpose: T16 anchor: a single live session that emits four distinct llm_error taxonomy values (rate_limit, context_overflow, authentication, timeout) plus an aborted streaming post_call. Drives the ERROR TYPE facet on Investigate (4 distinct pills) and the session-row red dot tooltip (4 distinct values listed). Coding agent only -- the other agents stay clean so T16 can assert the dot is selectively applied.

ancient-only.purpose: T5b anchor: agent whose only sessions are >7 days old, beyond the 7-day window that must not clip the expanded swimlane drawer. 9 days started, 8 days ended. Confirms the drawer surfaces these sessions. Used only on the dedicated ancient-agent fixture so the canonical pollution stays bounded. Requires post-seed SQL backdate AND force_state='closed' (worker stamps NOW() on every column write).

policy-active.purpose: T17 anchor: live session emitting one of each policy enforcement event type (policy_warn, policy_degrade, policy_block) so the drawer renders all three distinct badges/icons, the Investigate POLICY facet shows three pills with count=1 each, the session-row dot is severity-ranked to red (block > degrade > warn), and the multi-policy expanded grid asserts on from_model/to_model/intended_model. Coding agent only -- the other agents stay clean so T17 can assert the dot is selectively applied. Also carries one mcp_policy_user_remembered (a remembered MCP approval with permission_mode bypassPermissions) for T124, behind 25 history_padding tool_calls so T125's anchor is past the session's first 21 events.

claude-subagent.purpose: T28 anchor — Claude Code Task subagent. Child session_start carries agent_role='Explore' and parent_session_id pointing back at a Claude Code parent. T28 verifies the child swimlane row + relationship pill + parent-link surface. ``parent_role`` references which parent agent's session is referenced; resolved by seed.py to the concrete UUID.
claude-subagent.captured_input: Investigate the auth module and surface every place that calls AuthMiddleware.
claude-subagent.captured_output: Found 4 callers in src/api/auth.py; the entry point is server.go:142.

crewai-researcher.purpose: T29 anchor — CrewAI Researcher child. Pairs with crewai-writer under the same crewai-parent fixture so the parent's relationship pill renders '→ 2'.
crewai-researcher.captured_input: Gather sources for the quarterly report on Q3 token usage.
crewai-researcher.captured_output: Pulled 12 sources from internal Grafana dashboards + 3 external benchmarks.

crewai-writer.purpose: T29 anchor — CrewAI Writer child. See crewai-researcher comment.
crewai-writer.captured_input: Draft the Q3 token usage section using the Researcher's notes.
crewai-writer.captured_output: Drafted three paragraphs covering the 28% MoM growth + the spike on May 1.

langgraph-research-node.purpose: T30 anchor — LangGraph agent-bearing node 'research_node'. Pairs with langgraph-writer-node under the same langgraph-parent.
langgraph-research-node.captured_input: Research the latency spike on the ingest path between 04:00 and 05:00 UTC.
langgraph-research-node.captured_output: Identified a runaway worker on docker-workers-2; CPU saturation 04:14-04:42.

langgraph-writer-node.captured_input: Compose an incident note based on the research_node findings.
langgraph-writer-node.captured_output: Posted incident note INC-2026-148 summarising the worker saturation.

subagent-error.purpose: T40 (L8) anchor — sub-agent that ended in lost state. seed.py emits session_start with parent_session_id + agent_role but NO matching session_end so the worker's state-revival path lands on lost. Drives the red-dot row-level failure cue across Investigate / AgentTable / Swimlane per CONTRIBUTING.md L8.

subagent-overflow-input.purpose: T38 anchor — sub-agent with a >8 KiB incoming_message body. seed.py forces the content-overflow path: incoming_message.has_content=true on the wire and the full body lands in event_content. Drives the click-to-expand fetch via /v1/events/{id}/content.

depth-2-middle.purpose: T35 anchor — middle layer of a depth-2 tree. Itself a child of e2e-test-depth2-grand (the grandparent) AND a parent of depth-2-leaf. Drives the SubAgentsTab combined view.
depth-2-middle.captured_input: Coordinate two sub-tasks across the leaf agent.

depth-2-leaf.purpose: T35 anchor — leaf of a depth-2 tree. Child of depth-2-middle (which is itself a child of e2e-test-depth2-grand). Drives '+N more levels' depth-aware UX cues.

mcp-active.purpose: T25 anchor: live session that connected to two MCP servers (one stdio, one http) and emitted one event of each MCP type (mcp_tool_list, mcp_tool_call, mcp_resource_list, mcp_resource_read, mcp_prompt_list, mcp_prompt_get) plus one mcp_tool_call_failed (anchors T25-16 / D-MCP-FAIL — MCPErrorIndicator on a structured-error MCP row). The mcp_tool_call additionally has capture_prompts=True so the dashboard's MCPEventDetails shows arguments + result. context.mcp_servers carries both server fingerprints so the session-drawer MCP SERVERS panel and the Investigate MCP SERVER facet aggregation both have data to render. Sensor agent only — Python sensor emits all six; the Claude Code plugin emits MCP_TOOL_CALL only. Also carries the call_fields_post_call anchor for T121 (the event detail shows every per-call field) and the prompt_content_post_call anchor for T123 (per-box Pretty / Raw in the Prompts panel).

concurrent-run-a.purpose: T52 anchor — first of two concurrent runs under the same agent_id. Simulates a multi-pod K8s deployment with FLIGHTDECK_HOSTNAME collapsed across pods: both pods register the same agent identity and emit independent session_ids whose start/end intervals overlap. Drives the RunBracket offset (top anchor).

concurrent-run-b.purpose: T52 anchor — second of two concurrent runs under the same agent_id. Starts 100s after concurrent-run-a, both still active, so the brackets overlap on the timeline and stagger to opposite vertical anchors.

fresh-closed-in-window.purpose: RunBracket end-square anchor — closed run with BOTH started_at and ended_at inside the swimlane's default 1-minute window so the end-square glyph (■) has a position to render at. The other ``recent-closed`` role is older (started -10min), outside the 1-minute window; without this fixture no closed session's end-square ever materialises on the live page. seed.py forward-dates this row on every keep-alive cycle so it stays in window.

fresh-subagent-in-window.purpose: SubAgentConnector in-window anchor — sub-agent session_start inside the swimlane's default 1-minute window so the connector overlay has a parent-child pair whose first events are both in the visible domain. The other sub-agent fixtures (claude-subagent, crewai-*, langgraph-*, depth2-*, subagent-*) all started >120s ago so their session_start events fall outside the 1-minute window and the connector geometry skips them. seed.py forward-dates this row on every keep-alive cycle so it stays in window.
fresh-subagent-in-window.captured_input: Connector anchor — fresh sub-agent emitting in-window events.
fresh-subagent-in-window.captured_output: Sub-agent emitted three tool_call events; parent's spawn event circle anchored the connector.

connector-parent-fresh.purpose: Dedicated parent session for the SubAgentConnector in-window anchor. seed.py keeps this session's started_at and a fresh tool_call event in window on every keep-alive cycle so the connector geometry pass finds an in-window event on the parent endpoint. Decoupled from e2e-test-coding-agent's fresh-active session (which T14/T15/T16/T18 consume) so the keep-alive's connector-anchor refresh doesn't perturb those tests' specific event-count / event-ordering assertions.

fanout-coordinator.purpose: The fan-out coordinator's run (e2e-test-fanout@e2e-host-fanout). seed.py's fan-out refresh pins it active with started_at = NOW-40s in the same statement as its three worker runs, so all four share one NOW(), and posts its spawn tool_call at NOW-31s, one second before the workers start. Runs in the full seed and on every keep-alive cycle. T133 and T134 draw their connectors from it.

fanout-worker-1.purpose: First of three runs of the coordinator's 'worker' sub-agent, started together the way a Claude Code coordinator fans out same-role sub-agents. The fan-out refresh pins all three active with started_at = NOW-30s and posts one tool_call each at NOW-30s. Excluded from refresh_subagent_events so T56 never moves them.

fanout-worker-2.purpose: Second of the three worker runs started together (see fanout-worker-1).

fanout-worker-3.purpose: Third of the three worker runs started together (see fanout-worker-1).

fanout-worker-lost.purpose: An earlier worker run that went lost: started 2 h ago, last seen 1 h 55 min ago, ended_at NULL. Its events are posted inside that span (event_offset_floor_sec lifts the usual 1 h clamp; ingestion accepts up to 48 h back). Pinned once by the full seed; the keep-alive and T56's refresh_subagent_events leave it alone, so its extent never moves during a run.

concurrent-run-lost-earlier.purpose: T52 anchor: an earlier run of the concurrent-runs agent that went lost (started 2 h ago, last seen 1 h 55 min ago, ended_at NULL). It ends at its last signal, so it holds no lane when the two concurrent runs start; read as running forever, it pushed both of them to the bottom edge. Pinned once by the full seed.

lane-reuse-a.purpose: T136 anchor: run A of the lane-reuse agent, closed. B starts while A runs and C starts after A ends, so C takes A's freed track: at 5m A and C keep the top edge and B sits on the bottom edge. The lane pin keeps all three at their offsets on every keep-alive cycle.

lane-reuse-b.purpose: T136 anchor: run B of the lane-reuse agent, open from -120 s (see lane-reuse-a).

lane-reuse-c.purpose: T136 anchor: run C of the lane-reuse agent, open from -60 s, after run A ended at -90 s (see lane-reuse-a).

handoff-first.purpose: T138 anchor: the first run of a hand-off, closed at -15 s. The second run starts 3 ms before it ends, the overlap a worker's processing order can stamp, so the row stays one lane and reads end then start.

handoff-second.purpose: T138 anchor: the second run of the hand-off, open from 3 ms before the first run ends (see handoff-first).

long-closed.purpose: T139 anchor: a run that started 2 h ago and closed 10 s ago, so at 1m, 5m and 1h its start is before the window and only its end square shows.

short-closed.purpose: T142 anchor: a 2 s run, narrower on screen than its two glyphs at 5m and 1h, so its end square follows its start triangle past the run's end.

resumed-run.purpose: T141 anchor: a run that ended at -340 s and was resumed under the same session id at -60 s: two segments with a gap, each segment end drawn with its own square. The lane pin shifts its events with its row, so both segments keep their offsets; at 15m its first start leaves 500 s of the window for drift.

resumed-gap-run.purpose: T141 anchor: another run of the resumed agent that ran inside the resumed run's gap, so it shares the resumed run's track and the row stays one lane.

lost-earlier.purpose: T140 anchor: a run that went lost 1 h 55 min ago, before the 1h window, so it draws nothing.

lost-recent.purpose: T140 anchor: a lost run started 50 min ago and last seen 40 min ago: at 1h it ends at its last signal with a hollow square.

reaped-run.purpose: T140 anchor: a run the orphan-timeout reaper closed a minute ago, last seen 30 min ago: it ends at its last signal with a hollow square, not at the reap.

reaped-old-run.purpose: T143 anchor: a run that started 30 h ago, outside the Fleet's 24 h sessions page, was last seen 20 min ago and was closed by the orphan-timeout reaper 2 min ago. Only the agent's recent_sessions rollup carries it, so the swimlane learns of the reap from the rollup's close_reasons.

agents._comment: T28 child agent. agent_role 'Explore' lives on each session; the identity derivation yields a distinct agent_id because the agent_role joins the 6-tuple input.
T29 parent — Crew kickoff. Children (crewai-researcher / crewai-writer) reference this agent's fresh-active session as their parent_session_id.
T30 parent — LangGraph runner. Agent-bearing node children point at this agent's fresh-active session.
T40 (L8) anchor — sub-agent whose state ends in lost. seed.py force_state='lost' bakes the row state.
T38 anchor — sub-agent with a >8 KiB incoming_message body driving the content-overflow fetch path.
T35 grandparent — top of the depth-2 tree.

T52 anchor — single agent_id with two overlapping active sessions (simulates multi-pod K8s with FLIGHTDECK_HOSTNAME collapsed across pods). An earlier lost run ends at its last signal, so at 5m the two concurrent runs' start glyphs take the top and the bottom edge (see the run anchors in ARCHITECTURE.md).

Dedicated parent agent for the SubAgentConnector in-window anchor. Decoupled from e2e-test-coding-agent so the keep-alive's connector-anchor refresh emissions don't perturb T14/T15/T16/T18's specific event-ordering assertions on coding-agent's fresh-active session.

SubAgentConnector in-window anchor — sub-agent paired with e2e-test-connector-parent's connector-parent-fresh session so the connector overlay has a parent-child pair with both endpoints inside the swimlane's default 1-minute domain. Keeps the connector overlay rendering at least one Bezier path on the live page without the operator widening the time window.

Fan-out coordinator, named the way the Claude Code plugin names an agent ({user}@{host}). Listed before its worker so the coordinator's session exists when the workers' session_start carries its parent_session_id.

The coordinator's same-role sub-agent, named {parent}/{role} as the plugin names one: a single agent with an earlier lost run and three runs started together. T132 reads its name at the 460 px default; T133 and T134 use its connectors.
T136 anchor: three runs where the third takes the first one's freed track.
T138 anchor: one run hands off to the next, 3 ms of worker-clock overlap included.
T139 anchor: a closed run whose start is before every window.
T142 anchor: a 2 s closed run.
T141 anchor: a resumed run with a gap, and a run inside the gap.
T140 anchor: lost runs and a reaped run, each ending at its last signal.
T143 anchor: a reaped run older than the 24 h sessions page.
